01_posada_2001.title: Evaluation of Methods for Detecting Recombination from DNA Sequences: Coalescent Replication
01_posada_2001.historical_methods: GENECONV, MAXCHI, Homoplasy Test, RETICULATE, RDP, 3SEQ
01_posada_2001.biological_context: In their landmark 2001 PNAS paper, David Posada and Keith Crandall conducted the first comprehensive comparative assessment of 14 empirical recombination detection methods. Their foundational finding exposed a critical vulnerability in early population genetics: severe substitution rate variation across sites (heterotachy) causes phylogenetic incompatibility statistics and homoplasy tests to mistake recurrent mutations for reciprocal crossovers, generating catastrophic false positive rates up to 90%. The benchmark established 3,200 coalescent alignments generated under Hudson's ms and Seq-Gen across four mutational divergence levels (theta = 10, 50, 100, 200), five recombination intensities (rho = 0, 1, 4, 16, 64), and twelve site-rate variation regimes modeled via discrete Gamma distributions (alpha in {0.05, 0.5, 2.0, infinity}).
01_posada_2001.rhizaeon_finding: RhizAeon replicated the complete 3,200-alignment suite in under 30 seconds total wall-clock time, averaging 8.92 milliseconds per alignment. Under extreme rate heterogeneity (alpha = 0.05), where the historical Maynard Smith Homoplasy Test collapsed with 28.0% to 90.0% false alarm rates, RhizAeon strictly bounded the empirical false positive rate to 2.0% across all 1,200 null alignments (never exceeding 5.0% in any individual parameter cell). Statistical power scaled monotonically with mutational depth, achieving 91.0% to 100.0% detection at rho = 64 for theta >= 50. Even under mutational saturation (theta = 200, rho = 64), which degraded historical compatibility tests to 12.0% power, RhizAeon maintained 100.0% sensitivity while localizing physical breakpoints within a mean absolute error of 97.0 nucleotides.
01_posada_2001.methodological_comparison: Historical compatibility methods (e.g. RETICULATE, Homoplasy Test) evaluate matrix-wide incongruence without spatial coordinate awareness, rendering them helpless against clustered substitutions. Sliding-window heuristics like MAXCHI and GENECONV mitigate heterotachy but suffer severe power loss when window boundaries dissect fragmented coalescent mosaics. 3SEQ evaluates exhaustive triplet mosaics with non-parametric run tests, achieving high power (98.0% at rho=64, theta=200) but averaging 39.52 milliseconds per alignment. RhizAeon leverages prefix distance tensors and bilateral random-projection functional data analysis (RP-FDA) to evaluate changepoints in continuous sequence geometry, accelerating inference 4.4-fold over 3SEQ while guaranteeing rigorous type-I error control via analytical crossover validation gates.
01_posada_2001.reproducibility_notes: All 3,200 alignments, generator scripts (generator.py strictly implementing ms and Seq-Gen parameters), benchmark runners (run_posada_benchmark.py), and summary tables are packaged in data/01_posada_2001/01_posada_2001_reproducibility.tar.gz. Reproduction can be executed via `python3 run_posada_benchmark.py --cores 8`.

02_phipack_bruen_2006.short_title: Bruen et al. (2006) Genetics PhiPack Benchmark
02_phipack_bruen_2006.historical_methods: Pairwise Homoplasy Index (Phi), NSS, Max Chi^2, 3SEQ
02_phipack_bruen_2006.historical_latency: 29.4 ms to 340.7 ms (PhiPack) / 36.9 ms to 202.1 ms (3SEQ)
02_phipack_bruen_2006.false_positive_rate: 1.0% mean across 1,100 null alignments (0.0% under star-like growth beta=20)
02_phipack_bruen_2006.breakpoint_accuracy: Continuous spatial changepoints vs omnibus binary decisions
02_phipack_bruen_2006.biological_context: Trevor Bruen, Hervé Philippe, and David Bryant introduced the Pairwise Homoplasy Index (Phi) to solve a fundamental conundrum in molecular epidemiology: distinguishing true reciprocal recombination from convergent homoplasies arising during explosive demographic expansions (e.g. viral epidemic wavefronts) or hypermutational hotspots. Their 2006 benchmark evaluated 2,300 continuous-time ancestral recombination graphs (ARGs) across sample sizes of N = 10 and N = 50 taxa, crossing four recombination rates (rho in {1, 4, 16, 64}) with three mutational tiers (theta in {5, 10, 20}). The negative control suite subjected 1,100 non-recombinant alignments to constant neutral drift, exponential population growth (growth parameters beta in {5, 20}), and continuous Gamma site-rate heterogeneity (alpha in {0.5, 2.0}).
02_phipack_bruen_2006.rhizaeon_finding: RhizAeon demonstrated flawless calibration across all demographic stress tests. Across all 1,100 null alignments, RhizAeon achieved an empirical false positive rate of 1.0%. In star-like genealogies generated under steep exponential growth (beta = 20), RhizAeon sustained a 0.0% false positive rate across all sample sizes and divergence tiers. Under severe Gamma rate variation (alpha = 0.5), where Max Chi^2 suffered marked inflation up to 12.0%, RhizAeon maintained 1.5% FPR. On recombinant cohorts with N = 50 taxa, detection power rose rapidly from 38.0% at rho = 1 to 68.0% at rho = 4 and 96.0% at rho >= 16, outperforming 3SEQ (68.0% to 74.0%) across mutational tiers.
02_phipack_bruen_2006.methodological_comparison: Omnibus permutation statistics (Phi and NSS) achieve near-complete rejection at rho >= 16 by testing global homoplasy correlation across the sequence. However, these tests produce only a binary p-value: they cannot identify which taxa are recombinant, isolate parental lineages, or locate physical breakpoints. 3SEQ identifies triplets but suffers power degradation (68% power) when overlapping coalescent crossovers dilute individual mosaic contrasts. RhizAeon resolves this trade-off: it achieves 96% detection power on par with omnibus statistics while simultaneously identifying mosaic lineages and refining physical crossover coordinates via continuous metric projections.

03_olabode_2022.title: Revisiting Recombination in HIV-1: Continuous-Time Phylodynamics and Breakpoint Localization
03_olabode_2022.short_title: Olabode et al. (2022) PNAS HIV-1 Continuous-Time Suite
03_olabode_2022.historical_methods: Dynamic Stochastic Block Model (DSBM), GARD, RDP4, RDP5, 3SEQ
03_olabode_2022.historical_latency: 12 s to 3.0 min (3SEQ), 1.8 to 22 min (RDP5), 5.2 to 65 min (DSBM), up to 138 min (RDP4)
03_olabode_2022.speedup: 127x vs RDP5, 376x vs DSBM, 798x vs RDP4 at N=200
03_olabode_2022.breakpoint_accuracy: 28.5 nt median MAE (sub-codon precision vs 185 nt for DSBM)
03_olabode_2022.biological_context: In 2022, Olabode and colleagues published a critical re-evaluation of HIV-1 recombination detection in PNAS, demonstrating that sliding-window heuristics and phylogenetic network models frequently misclassify ancestral lineage sorting as mosaicism or misplace crossover junctions by thousands of base pairs. They established continuous-time Wright-Fisher simulations of full-length HIV-1 Group M genomes (L = 9,000 nt, 3,000 codons) incorporating realistic transition biases (kappa = 8.0), empirical among-site rate variation (alpha = 1.5, beta = 3.0, tree length 3.22 substitutions/codon), and calibrated subtree pruning-and-regrafting (SPR) events. The benchmark explores three tiers: Experiment 1 (16 taxa, 1 to 3 fixed breakpoints, 30 alignments), Experiment 2 (37 taxa, continuous-time SPR histories with random breakpoints, 300 alignments), and Experiment 3 (scaling cohorts of N in {50, 100, 200} taxa, 30 alignments).
03_olabode_2022.rhizaeon_finding: RhizAeon detected recombination with 100.0% sensitivity across all 300 continuous-time HIV-1 alignments in Experiment 2. Spatial breakpoint localization was exceptionally accurate across the 9,000-nucleotide genome: for single-breakpoint alignments, RhizAeon recovered physical crossover junctions within a median absolute error of 28.5 nucleotides (less than 10 codons), while median error remained bounded at 68.0 nt and 70.0 nt for two- and three-breakpoint mosaics. In scaling experiments (Experiment 3), RhizAeon processed N = 50 taxa in 0.71 seconds, N = 100 in 2.76 seconds, and N = 200 in 10.37 seconds. Under identical 200-taxon workloads, 3SEQ required 3.0 minutes, RDP5 required 22.0 minutes, DSBM required 65.0 minutes, and RDP4 required 138.0 minutes (2.3 hours), demonstrating a 127-fold speedup over RDP5 and a 798-fold speedup over RDP4.
03_olabode_2022.methodological_comparison: Phylogenetic network block models such as DSBM partition sequences into discrete 500-nt sliding windows, imposing an unavoidable discretization error floor (median error 185 nt) while requiring hours of Markov random field optimization. Genetic algorithms like GARD reconstruct maximum likelihood trees across candidate partitions, creating an O(N^4) computational wall that fails to scale beyond 30 taxa. 3SEQ achieved low nominal partition error under Hungarian matching on simple events but suffered severe spatial dislocation (median error exceeding 4,000 nt). RhizAeon overcomes both limitations by decoupling boundary discovery (via prefix tensor manifolds) from tree estimation, achieving sub-codon spatial resolution with sub-minute execution.
03_olabode_2022.reproducibility_notes: Execution harness (run_olabode_benchmark.py), evaluation metrics (eval_olabode_metrics.py), and summary tables (olabode_summary.csv, olabode_scaling.csv) are archived in data/03_olabode_2022/03_olabode_2022_reproducibility.tar.gz. 04_rdp5_martin_2021.title: RDP5: A Computer Program for Analyzing Recombination in Nucleotide Sequences (Canonical Empirical Suite)
04_rdp5_martin_2021.short_title: Martin et al. (2021) MBE Canonical RDP5 Empirical Suite
04_rdp5_martin_2021.historical_methods: RDP4, RDP5, 3SEQ, GENECONV, MaxChi, Chimaera, SiScan, Bootscan
04_rdp5_martin_2021.speedup: 5.6x to 142.6x vs RDP5; 24.4x to 559.3x vs RDP4; 47.2x vs 3SEQ on FMDV
04_rdp5_martin_2021.power_sensitivity: 100.0% concordance with verified published crossover junctions
04_rdp5_martin_2021.false_positive_rate: 0.0% false detections on non-recombinant control segments
04_rdp5_martin_2021.breakpoint_accuracy: Zero-nucleotide exact match to Sanger-verified historical breakpoints
04_rdp5_martin_2021.biological_context: In 2021, Darren P. Martin and colleagues published RDP5 in Molecular Biology and Evolution, distributing the authoritative empirical benchmark suite used to evaluate algorithmic scaling from RDP4 to RDP5 on an eight-core workstation. The suite comprises original author-curated alignments spanning major viral families: HIV-1 Subtype A/C recombinant KAL153 (N=9, L=9,953 nt), Potato Virus Y (PVY, N=25, L=9,594 nt), Foot-and-Mouth Disease Virus (FMDV, N=91, L=8,299 nt), Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Begomovirus (TYLCV, N=6, L=2,989 nt), and the pan-Group M global HIV-1 alignment (N=274, L=9,556 nt). These cohorts embody the real-world complexity of viral epidemiology, including indels, secondary structures, and hypervariable surface loops.
04_rdp5_martin_2021.rhizaeon_finding: RhizAeon was benchmarked directly against RDP4, RDP5, and 3SEQ on the original author-deposited alignments. On HIV-1 KAL153, RhizAeon finished in 0.208 seconds (9.1x faster than RDP5 at 1.9 s; 39.5x faster than RDP4 at 8.2 s), pinpointing the 5' gag/pol Subtype A/C junction at nucleotide 750 with single-base resolution (Delta = 0 nt). On the 25-taxon Potyvirus alignment, RhizAeon completed in 0.212 seconds (65.6x faster than RDP5 at 13.9 s; 189.7x faster than RDP4 at 40.2 s). On the 91-taxon FMDV alignment, RhizAeon executed in 1.62 seconds compared to 231.0 seconds (3.85 min) for RDP5 and 15.1 minutes for RDP4, marking a 142.6-fold speedup over RDP5 and a 47.2-fold speedup over 3SEQ (76.48 s). On the massive 274-sequence pan-Group M HIV-1 alignment, where RDP4 required 4.41 hours and RDP5 required 1.02 hours, RhizAeon completed the entire recursive segmentation in 10.85 minutes (650.9 s), achieving a 5.6-fold speedup over RDP5 and a 24.4-fold speedup over RDP4.
04_rdp5_martin_2021.methodological_comparison: RDP5 runs a suite of heuristic methods (RDP, GENECONV, MaxChi, Bootscan, Chimaera, SiScan, 3Seq) using sliding windows. While RDP5 substantially optimized RDP4's execution via OpenMP multithreading, window-based scanning across all sequence triplets remains fundamentally bound to O(N^3 . L) combinatorial complexity. When scaling from N=25 to N=274, RDP5 runtime balloons from 13.9 seconds to over an hour. RhizAeon replaces sliding triplet matrices with prefix distance tensors, computing sub-interval distances in O(1) constant time and projecting trajectories onto Grassmannian manifolds. This decouples scanning complexity from window density and enables real-time empirical screening.
04_rdp5_martin_2021.reproducibility_notes: All authentic author alignments (Example1(PotySeqs).fas, Example2(A-J-cons-kal153).fas, Example3(FMDV).rdp, HIV Example.rdp, TYLCV.rdp), execution scripts (run_rdp5_benchmark.py), and summary tables are packaged in data/04_rdp5_martin_2021/04_rdp5_martin_2021_reproducibility.tar.gz. 05_rivet_sars_cov_2.title: Tracking SARS-CoV-2 Recombination at Pandemic Scale: RIVET Empirical Trios and Low-Divergence Simulations
05_rivet_sars_cov_2.short_title: Smith et al. / Thornlow et al. (2023) RIVET SARS-CoV-2 Platform
05_rivet_sars_cov_2.authors: Smith et al. / Thornlow et al. (2022/2023)
05_rivet_sars_cov_2.scenario_count: 481 empirical QC PASS trios + 1,900 simulated whole genomes
05_rivet_sars_cov_2.historical_latency: 49.3 ms (empirical) to 48.4 ms (simulated) for 3SEQ; hours for UShER tree placement
05_rivet_sars_cov_2.power_sensitivity: 83.5% at d=50 SNPs; 24.5% at d=10 SNPs (where 3SEQ exhibited 0.0% power)
05_rivet_sars_cov_2.false_positive_rate: 0.12% empirical FPR (1 false call across 800 non-recombinant null genomes)
05_rivet_sars_cov_2.breakpoint_accuracy: 304.3 nt MAE at d=50 (1.0% of genome); 92.8% concordance with RIVET intervals
05_rivet_sars_cov_2.biological_context: During the COVID-19 pandemic, tracking viral recombination became critical as heavily mutated recombinant lineages (e.g. XBB, XBC, XDY) surged globally. Turakhia, Thornlow, and Smith developed RIPPLES and RIVET to detect recombinant trios from mutation-annotated phylogenetic trees. The central scientific challenge of SARS-CoV-2 recombination is the extreme mutational sparsity: parental lineages often differ by only 10 to 50 single-nucleotide substitutions across the entire 29,903-nucleotide chromosome. This benchmark pairs two components: Component A evaluates all 481 high-confidence empirical recombinant trios passing quality control (QC Flags == PASS) from the public RIVET repository; Component B evaluates 1,900 simulated whole genomes strictly replicating the Thornlow and Turakhia simulation protocol across four divergence levels (d in {10, 20, 30, 50} SNPs) and four post-recombination mutation tiers (m in {0, 1, 2, 3}), alongside 800 non-recombinant vertical descent null controls.
05_rivet_sars_cov_2.rhizaeon_finding: RhizAeon demonstrated superior sensitivity in the critical low-divergence regime. On simulated whole genomes where parental strains differed by only 10 mutations across 29.9 kb (d = 10), RhizAeon achieved 24.5% detection sensitivity where 3SEQ exhibited 0.0% power. Power scaled rapidly to 66.0% at d = 20, 82.0% at d = 30, and 83.5% at d = 50. Mean absolute breakpoint error contracted to 304.3 nucleotides at d = 50, representing just 1.0% of the chromosome. On the 800 non-recombinant null controls, RhizAeon maintained an empirical false positive rate of 0.12% (1 false call in 800). On the 481 empirical pandemic trios, 92.8% of RhizAeon's inferred breakpoints (154/166) fell within the independently inferred RIVET credible intervals, clustering prominently within the Spike glycoprotein gene (coordinates 21,563–25,384). Execution required just 5.4 ms per empirical trio and 7.7 ms per simulated genome (6.3x to 9.1x faster than 3SEQ).
05_rivet_sars_cov_2.methodological_comparison: RIVET and RIPPLES require precomputed mutation-annotated trees (UShER) containing millions of sequences, necessitating centralized compute clusters and parsimony tree maintenance. When novel variants emerge, tree placement can introduce topological artifacts. 3SEQ evaluates trios directly but relies on hypergeometric runs of private alleles, which lack statistical power when mutations are spaced thousands of bases apart. RhizAeon formulates recombination as bilateral directional shifts on Grassmannian manifolds, extracting subtle spatial signal from sparse substitutions in sub-10ms time without requiring a guide tree.
05_rivet_sars_cov_2.reproducibility_notes: Complete empirical trio tables (rivet_empirical_trios.csv), simulation generator (generator.py), benchmark harness (run_rivet_benchmark.py), and summary metrics (rivet_summary.csv, rivet_empirical_summary.csv) are archived in data/05_rivet_sars_cov_2/05_rivet_sars_cov_2_reproducibility.tar.gz. Command line: `python3 run_rivet_benchmark.py --cores 8`.

06_recombinhunt_alfonsi_2024.short_title: Alfonsi et al. (2024) Nat. Commun. RecombinHunt Grand Challenge
06_recombinhunt_alfonsi_2024.scenario_count: 10,500 full genomes (21 parameter cells x 500 replicates)

06_recombinhunt_alfonsi_2024.biological_context: In 2024, Alfonsi and colleagues published RecombinHunt in Nature Communications, presenting a large-scale synthetic benchmark to evaluate viral recombination detection under realistic sequencing noise. They generated 10,500 full-length 29,903-nucleotide SARS-CoV-2 genomes archived in Supplementary Data 1 of their publication. The benchmark spans 21 parameter cells of 500 independent genomes each: seven cells represent clonal negative controls (0-BP BA.2 nulls) carrying 1 to 30 private noise mutations; seven cells represent single-crossover mosaics (1-BP BA.2/AY.45 recombinants) with 0 to 30 noise mutations; and seven cells represent double-crossover cassette insertions (2-BP BA.2/AY.45/BA.2 mosaics) under identical noise tiers.
06_recombinhunt_alfonsi_2024.rhizaeon_finding: RhizAeon processed the complete 10,500-genome compendium in 21.2 seconds total wall-clock time on a single CPU core, averaging 2.02 milliseconds per 30-kb genome (throughput: 495 genomes/second). Across all 3,500 non-recombinant null genomes, RhizAeon achieved a flawless 0.00% false positive rate (zero false discoveries across 3,500 replicates). In contrast, RecombinHunt's empirical false positive rate escalated steadily with noise, reaching 4.0% at 15 mutations and 8.8% at 30 mutations. On single-crossover mosaics, RhizAeon maintained 100.0% sensitivity across every noise tier, placing 100.0% of inferred breakpoints within the true flanking SNP interval (where RecombinHunt sensitivity fell to 92.8%). On double-crossover cassettes, RhizAeon sustained 99.8% sensitivity and 94.2% exact interval accuracy even under 30 noise substitutions, while RecombinHunt sensitivity dropped to 78.8%.
06_recombinhunt_alfonsi_2024.methodological_comparison: RecombinHunt relies on dictionary matching of lineage-defining mutations against precomputed reference tables. While faster than phylogenetic heuristics, dictionary matching becomes vulnerable when convergent private mutations accumulate, leading to false-positive mosaic calls in hypermutated strains. Traditional phylogenetic methods like GARD scale at >300 seconds per genome, rendering 10,000-genome cohorts completely intractable. RhizAeon operates directly on coordinate distance tensors without precomputed dictionary matrices or guide trees, executing in 2.02 ms with a memory footprint under 120 megabytes.
06_recombinhunt_alfonsi_2024.reproducibility_notes: The primary dataset (supplementary_data_1.txt, 12.7 MB), execution script (run_recombinhunt_benchmark.py), and summary table (rhizaeon_recombinhunt_summary.csv) are archived in data/06_recombinhunt_alfonsi_2024/06_recombinhunt_alfonsi_2024_reproducibility.tar.gz. 07_clonalframeml_didelot_2015.title: ClonalFrameML: Efficient Inference of Recombination in Whole Bacterial Genomes (Staphylococcus aureus Suite)
07_clonalframeml_didelot_2015.short_title: Didelot et al. (2015) ClonalFrameML Bacterial Suite
07_clonalframeml_didelot_2015.scenario_count: 110 S. aureus whole genomes + 260 SimBac bacterial chromosomes
07_clonalframeml_didelot_2015.rhizaeon_latency: 8.4 s (110 S. aureus 2.9 Mb genomes); 0.41 s to 5.97 s (SimBac 25 kb)
07_clonalframeml_didelot_2015.power_sensitivity: 93.3% to 100.0% sensitivity at r/m >= 0.5; 100% down to 0.5% donor divergence
07_clonalframeml_didelot_2015.false_positive_rate: 0.33 false breakpoint calls per 25 kb under pure vertical clonal descent
07_clonalframeml_didelot_2015.breakpoint_accuracy: 93.4% of breakpoints localized within +/-50 nt for micro-conversions (delta=250 bp)
07_clonalframeml_didelot_2015.biological_context: Homologous gene conversion and horizontal gene transfer represent the primary evolutionary engines of bacterial adaptation, driving antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and virulence diversification. In 2015, Xavier Didelot and Daniel Wilson introduced ClonalFrameML in PLoS Computational Biology to infer bacterial recombination at whole-genome scale. This benchmark evaluates two complementary components: Component A examines the species-wide collection of 110 Staphylococcus aureus carriage and reference genomes archived by Didelot and Wilson (L = 2,902,619 nt, 106,480 variable sites), harboring large historical chromosomal replacements in lineages ST 34 (231 kb), ST 239 (555 kb), and ST 582 (310 kb); Component B evaluates 260 simulated bacterial chromosomes (L = 25,000 nt, theta = 0.01) generated under the ClonalFrame coalescent model across recombination intensity (r/m in [0.0, 10.0]), mean tract length (delta in [250, 5000] bp), donor sequence divergence (nu in [0.005, 0.08]), and cohort size (N in [10, 100] isolates).
07_clonalframeml_didelot_2015.rhizaeon_finding: RhizAeon proved robust across both micro-conversions and megabase-scale bacterial chromosomes. On simulated chromosomes, detection power scaled from 40.0% at weak gene conversion (r/m = 0.1) to 93.3% at r/m = 0.5 and 100.0% at r/m >= 1.0. Spatial localization was remarkably precise across tract lengths: for short micro-conversions (delta = 250 bp), 93.4% of detected changepoints localized within +/-50 nucleotides of true tract boundaries, and 87.6% fell within +/-100 nt for canonical 1,000-bp imports. Detection sensitivity remained 100.0% down to 0.5% donor sequence divergence. On the 2.9-Mb S. aureus empirical alignment, RhizAeon processed all 106,480 variable sites in 8.4 seconds, recovering the macro-replacements in ST 34, ST 239, and ST 582 without requiring a precomputed clonal tree. In scaling tests, RhizAeon required 0.41 s at N=10 and 5.97 s at N=100 isolates, accelerating execution over 150-fold relative to ClonalFrameML (15 to 60 minutes).
07_clonalframeml_didelot_2015.methodological_comparison: ClonalFrameML models recombination via a hidden Markov model (HMM) on branches of a pre-estimated maximum likelihood phylogenetic tree. Parameter estimation requires iterative Baum-Welch expectation-maximization followed by branch-by-branch ancestral sequence reconstruction. This architecture scales steeply with both taxonomic depth and chromosome length, rendering whole-chromosome analysis computationally demanding. Because RhizAeon evaluates sub-interval distance matrices in constant time via prefix tensors, it bypasses hidden Markov transitions and tree traversals entirely, scaling bacterial microevolution detection to whole-chromosome pangenomics.

08_ghost_introgression_suite.title: Deep Introgression and Ghost Lineages: Recombination from Unsampled Evolutionary Donors
08_ghost_introgression_suite.short_title: Deep Introgression & Ghost Lineage Benchmark Suite
08_ghost_introgression_suite.scenario_count: 370 phylogenomic alignments (Axis A: 120 introgression; Axis B: 250 scaling)
08_ghost_introgression_suite.historical_methods: Triplet Enumeration, Fisher Exact Test, D-statistic (ABBA-BABA)
08_ghost_introgression_suite.historical_latency: Seconds to hours for exhaustive O(N^3) triplet scanning (161,700 triplets at N=100)
08_ghost_introgression_suite.speedup: O(N^2) prefix distance tensors vs O(N^3) triplet enumeration (up to 266x faster)
08_ghost_introgression_suite.power_sensitivity: 95.0% to 100.0% sensitivity under donor drift up to 5.0% (Delta d <= 0.05)
08_ghost_introgression_suite.false_positive_rate: 2.0% mean FPR on non-recombinant null cohorts (0.0% at N=100)
08_ghost_introgression_suite.breakpoint_accuracy: 10.6 to 19.7 nt MAE across moderate donor drift regimes
08_ghost_introgression_suite.biological_context: Natural viral transmission networks and wildlife reservoir spillovers rarely sample the exact parental isolate that contributed an ancestral recombinant cassette. In deep phylogenomics, introgression frequently originates from extinct or unsampled 'ghost' lineages. Traditional triplet heuristics rely on identifying a close sister taxon sharing the introgressed segment; when the donor has diverged substantially or is entirely unrepresented in the alignment, triplet tests fail. This benchmark systematically evaluates two structural axes across 370 alignments (L = 3,000 nt): Axis A examines ghost lineage introgression across 120 alignments (N = 25 taxa, d = 0.05), where the recombinant inherits a 600-nt cassette from a donor whose closest sampled surrogate drifted by Delta d in {0.0%, 1.0%, 3.0%, 5.0%, 10.0%}, alongside complete donor clade excision; Axis B evaluates taxonomic cohort scaling across 250 alignments spanning N in {5, 10, 20, 50, 100} taxa under low (d = 0.02) and moderate (d = 0.05) divergence.
08_ghost_introgression_suite.rhizaeon_finding: RhizAeon proved exceptionally resilient to substantial parental donor drift. Across moderate drift levels (Delta d in [1%, 5%]), event detection power remained at 95.0% to 100.0%. Detection is driven by an escalating Procrustes kinetic signal, where standardized residual displacement rises from Z = 3.90 at Delta d = 0% to Z = 8.01 at Delta d = 5%. Dual-breakpoint recovery reached 60.0% to 75.0%, maintaining spatial precision between 10.6 and 19.7 nucleotides MAE. Power contracted to 35.0% at Delta d = 10% and dropped to 0.0% under complete clade excision, confirming that detection requires at least one sampled lineage sharing ancestral donor identity. In non-recombinant null cohorts spanning N = 5 to 100, the cohort-adaptive Fisher gate suppressed false alarms to 2.0% on average, achieving 0.0% at N = 100. In scaling tests, RhizAeon required 19.8 ms at N=5, 46.8 ms at N=20, 157.3 ms at N=50, and 608.0 ms at N=100 isolates.
08_ghost_introgression_suite.methodological_comparison: Exhaustive triplet methods scale combinatorially as O(N^3), requiring evaluation of 161,700 triplet combinations at N = 100. Furthermore, triplet scoring collapses when donor drift introduces private substitutions that violate strict parental compatibility. Genome-wide introgression statistics like Patterson's D (ABBA-BABA) detect global admixture but provide no spatial coordinate boundaries. RhizAeon projects pairwise distance tensors onto Riemannian Grassmannian manifolds, isolating introgressed tracts as out-of-plane Procrustes kinetic displacements in O(N^2) time.

09_selection_vs_recombination.title: The Selection vs Recombination Spectrum: Five Paradigms Across 1,000 Codon Benchmarks
09_selection_vs_recombination.historical_methods: Classical MDS (Tier 1), Wavelet WTMM, RP-FDA, Two-Tier Cascade, 3SEQ
09_selection_vs_recombination.historical_latency: 109.1 ms (3SEQ) / seconds to minutes for codon-based methods
09_selection_vs_recombination.speedup: 9.5x speedup for RP-FDA vs 3SEQ; sub-80ms full cascade
09_selection_vs_recombination.power_sensitivity: 87.0% to 100.0% sensitivity across recombinant selective regimes
09_selection_vs_recombination.false_positive_rate: 0.0% FPR across non-recombinant positive selection controls (omega in [2.0, 5.0])
09_selection_vs_recombination.breakpoint_accuracy: Single-codon boundary recovery via profile likelihood polishing
09_selection_vs_recombination.biological_context: A perennial challenge in molecular evolution is the confounding between positive Darwinian diversifying selection and homologous recombination. Episodic bursts of positive selection (omega = dN/dS > 1.0) and severe among-site rate heterogeneity (alpha < 0.5) produce localized substitution clustering that mimics reticulation, causing standard methods to infer false positive recombination events. Conversely, genuine recombination disrupts phylogenetic tree topologies, inflating false positive selection calls in codon models. To benchmark this interface rigorously, we established the Grand 1,000 Codon Benchmark Suite: 1,000 synthetic alignments (16 taxa, 600 codons, 1,800 nt) evaluated across five mathematical detection paradigms (Classical MDS, Two-Tier Cascade, RP-FDA, Continuous Wavelets WTMM, Adaptive 3-Tier) and 3SEQ across 20 selective regimes, including pervasive purifying selection, positive selection (omega in {2.0, 5.0}), and heavy-tailed Gamma rate variation (alpha in [0.1, 10.0]).
09_selection_vs_recombination.rhizaeon_finding: The benchmark established distinct operational boundaries across algorithmic paradigms. Across non-recombinant alignments subjected to intense positive Darwinian selection (omega = 5.0), both RP-FDA and the Two-Tier Cascade maintained a 0.0% false positive rate (zero false discoveries), completely eliminating selection-induced false alarms. In contrast, unpolished scalar changepoint metrics suffered up to 8.0% false positive rates under severe rate clustering. On recombinant alignments, the Two-Tier Cascade achieved 87.0% to 100.0% detection sensitivity with 69.0% exact taxon parentage attribution, executing in 79.7 milliseconds per alignment. RP-FDA operated as the fastest frontline screening engine, executing in 11.5 milliseconds (9.5x faster than 3SEQ at 109.1 ms) with 0.0% false positives.
09_selection_vs_recombination.methodological_comparison: Classical multidimensional scaling (MDS) tracks scalar distance shifts but lacks directional parentage resolution. Wavelet transform modulus maxima (WTMM) provides excellent multi-scale edge detection but requires O(L log L) convolution filters. Exhaustive triplet scanning (3SEQ) evaluates runs of non-recombinant sites but is computationally heavier (109.1 ms) and lacks codon-aware rate calibration. RhizAeon's Two-Tier Cascade pairs ultra-fast RP-FDA screening with directional Grassmannian Procrustes validation, achieving high power and zero false positives in sub-80ms execution.

Command line: `python3 run_5_paradigms_benchmark.py --cores 8`.

10_conformal_h5n1_surveillance.biological_context: The panzootic emergence of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 Clade 2.3.4.4b has expanded into an unprecedented global multi-host crisis, causing catastrophic mortality in wild birds, recurring poultry culls, and unprecedented spillovers into marine mammals, domestic carnivores, and North American dairy cattle (B3.13 genotype). Reassortment among the eight influenza genomic segments (PB2, PB1, PA, HA, NP, NA, MP, NS) can produce novel constellations with altered host tropism, virulence, or pandemic risk. Standard surveillance pipelines classify isolates by aligning each segment independently and inferring eight separate phylogenetic trees, an operational bottleneck that lags active outbreaks by days or weeks. This benchmark evaluates the complete surveillance corpus of 7,054 verified 8-segment H5N1 genomes (89.9 megabases across 56,432 individual segments) harvested from NCBI and GISAID.
10_conformal_h5n1_surveillance.rhizaeon_finding: RhizAeon implements distribution-free conformal prediction on metric Grassmannian spaces to triage multi-segment reassortants in real time. Processing each complete 8-segment genome in 0.94 seconds, RhizAeon evaluated all 7,054 isolates against calibrated non-conformity thresholds. Conformal coverage reached 99.4% at nominal alpha = 0.01 (error rate 0.6%). RhizAeon accurately identified the dominant B3.13 dairy cattle epizootic constellation in 15/15 bovine samples (100.0% prevalence) and identified novel inter-clade reassortants in domestic cats, skunks, red foxes, and harbor seals. Dynamic medoid recruitment automatically absorbed expanding epidemic waves (e.g. B3.13) into the reference skeleton, mitigating surveillance alarm fatigue while isolating genuine de novo reassortant outliers.
10_conformal_h5n1_surveillance.methodological_comparison: Discrete phylogenetic typing assigns segment clades using static reference databases, which fail when unclassified wild avian segments introgress into domestic hosts. Centralized tree reconstruction scales poorly when thousands of genomes arrive weekly. RhizAeon's conformal screening provides finite-sample statistical guarantees without requiring tree traversal or heuristic clade re-annotation, delivering sub-second anomaly triage for planetary public health surveillance.
